title: Tag each item's standard in its data
statement: Tag every item with the standard it measures in its structured data, not in a title or the item text, using one code convention that resolves in the official framework.
example: One audited test carried standards on 0 of its 28 items, with the codes only in titles.
detail: A course check found standards on 0 of 28 items of one test, with the codes only in titles (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/BRIEFING.md`), and a pull of another live course found no standards field on any of its 1,026 items and just 3 codes in the whole file, all in lesson titles (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0082-rex-v2-live-course-pull-2026-07-02-rex-v2-live-course-pull.qmd`). The staged integration standard keeps standards in structured metadata, never only inside the item markup, which once caused a false zero on pull, and asks for one code convention, normalized so nothing is counted twice (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/timeback-integration.md`).

evidence.quote: **No item in this dump carries any standards field.**
Standards live in **`metadata`, never inline in `rawXml`.** A rawXml-only authoring shortcut produces a false-zero on pull (this caused a spurious "zero standards" FAIL pre-re-pull).
Human codes (`RI.3.1`, `CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.RI.3.1`) are accepted but **pick one convention** and normalize (`CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.` → bare code) so the reader doesn't double-count.
